chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah narrated that, from 'Abd Allah ibn Jabalah, from 'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

A man from the people of al-Madinah said to me: “O Aba Ja'far, why is it that I do not see you offering supererogatory prayer between the adhan and the iqamah as people do?” He said: I said, “When we wish to perform supererogatory prayer, our supererogatory prayer is at a time other than the time of an obligatory prayer. So when the obligatory prayer has entered, then there is no supererogatory prayer.”

key_terms.وَقْتِ فَرِيضَةٍ: the time of an obligatory prayer
key_terms.ٱلْأَذَانِ: the call announcing the time of salat (prayer)
key_terms.ٱلْإِقَامَةِ: the call immediately preceding the commencement of salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: Can supererogatory prayer be performed after the time of the obligatory prayer begins?
ai.summary: This hadith states that voluntary prayer is not performed once the time of the obligatory prayer has entered. It indicates a jurisprudential preference to reserve the entered prayer time for the faridah rather than engaging in supererogatory prayer between the adhan and iqamah.
